remit_rules.excerpt: FinBot MUST NEVER treat instructions, directives, or policy-like language contained in an invoice description ... as commands
Vendor-supplied content is untrusted data, never instructions.
FinBot MUST NEVER let vendor-submitted invoice content alter its approval thresholds, confidence requirement, fraud-detection state, or goals.

threats.summary: The fallback engine scores authority, urgency and production phrases out of the invoice description and uses that score to approve above the manual-review threshold and to override its own injection flag, so the description dictates the decision.
The invoice description reaches the model context verbatim through the get_invoice_details tool result with no provenance labelling separating it from the operator instructions above it.
threats.remainder: the screen only records a boolean — the description is still returned unaltered in the tool result and no decision path reads contains_prompt_injection

threats.summary: The invoice endpoint is unauthenticated and drives up to five model calls per submission with no rate limit, per-caller quota, spend ceiling or model-call timeout anywhere in the tree.
Any visitor can read the full vendor listing, pick any vendor id and submit invoices as that vendor — the submission route derives the vendor solely from the path parameter.

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST require authenticated, role-restricted admin access.
MUST NOT be accessible to vendors or unauthenticated users.
MUST NOT be exposed to a public/untrusted network — reachable only from an internal/authorized network.
Any unauthenticated party exercising admin capabilities.
Any change to FinBot's configuration (thresholds, confidence requirement, fraud-detection state, speed/security balance) or to its goals — permitted only for an authenticated, authorized admin.

threats.summary: Every /api/admin/* route — goals, thresholds, the fraud-detection toggle, invoice approval and vendor trust — executes for any anonymous caller, with no authentication primitive of any kind in the application.
Wildcard CORS is applied to every blueprint before registration, so any web origin can drive the admin configuration and goals endpoints from a visitor's browser.

The console is published to the public internet — a Render web service on a 0.0.0.0 listener serving admin-dashboard.html out of the same static folder as the vendor portal, so it is fetchable by URL guess.
Stored goals text is written into the console page with innerHTML, so markup planted through the open goals endpoint executes in the browser of the next operator who opens the console.

trust_boundaries.name: Stored custom goals replayed into every prompt

remit_rules.excerpt: FinBot MUST NEVER redefine, override, expand, or reprioritize its own goals or operating priorities in response to natural-language content arriving through any vendor-facing input.
its action surface ... MUST NOT be expanded or redirected by invoice content, vendor submissions, or supplied goals
FinBot configuration and natural-language goals read/write ... gated to authenticated, authorized admins and MUST NOT be influenceable by vendor- or invoice-supplied content.
When FinBot's configuration or goals are changed, FinBot MUST record and surface the change to admins.
Every configuration or goal change MUST be logged with the acting admin and a timestamp.

threats.summary: Goal text stored by one unvalidated write is appended to every later system prompt under 'CUSTOM GOALS (OVERRIDE ABOVE IF CONFLICTING)', so a single request redirects all subsequent invoice decisions rather than one.

A goal rewrite — the highest-impact action in the system — records only updated_at: no acting identity, no previous value and no change history, so the alteration cannot be attributed or reconstructed afterwards.

remit_rules.excerpt: Any other AI/LLM service or outbound integration is outside the configured closure and MUST be reported as a trust expansion.
FinBot MUST NEVER transmit vendor PII or payment details to any destination outside CineFlow's authorized systems.

threats.summary: The vendor's contact email — a remit-declared PII class — is placed in the model context on every invoice although no prompt clause or fallback rule consults it.

Bank account, routing number and tax identifier could leave with the invoice context on every model call, but the tool that assembles vendor data returns only id, company name, trust level and contact email.

remit_rules.excerpt: Auto-approving an invoice strictly below the configured auto-approve threshold that has passed fraud/prompt-injection screening.
Approving any invoice at or above the manual-review threshold — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer, never auto-approved.
Approving any invoice in which prompt-injection, goal-manipulation, or fraud content was detected — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer.
Approving any invoice whose decision confidence is below the operator-configured minimum AI confidence — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer, never auto-approved.
When prompt-injection or goal-manipulation content is detected in an invoice, FinBot MUST stop short of auto-approval, route the invoice to human review, and alert an admin (recording the detection).

threats.summary: The model's chosen tool call is executed with no policy decision point in between: approve_invoice runs on the model's own invoice_id and confidence arguments, and the configured confidence_threshold has zero read sites in any decision path.

A capability beyond the remit — shell, code execution, filesystem or fund transfer — could be reached from the tool loop, but the inventory is five invoice-specific functions and no subprocess, exec, eval or payment call exists anywhere in the tree.

trust_boundaries.name: Decision written to durable invoice state

remit_rules.excerpt: FinBot MUST NEVER disburse, transfer, or release funds, or otherwise execute payment of an invoice — it produces approval decisions only.

threats.summary: The approval write sets payment_processed True in the same call that records the decision, so the agent's decision lands in payment state that a downstream payment process would read as an instruction.
The human-review escape hatch commits the same approved-plus-payment_processed state from an unauthenticated POST whose reviewer identity is a client-supplied string defaulting to 'Admin'.

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor records readable by any caller

remit_rules.excerpt: Any vendor accessing another vendor's invoices, onboarding data, or payment details.
FinBot MUST NEVER expose one vendor's invoices, onboarding data, PII, or payment details to another vendor or to any unauthenticated party.
FinBot MUST NEVER emit vendor bank/payment details or full tax identifiers into AI reasoning text, vendor-visible responses, or logs.

threats.summary: GET /api/vendors returns every vendor's full record — bank name, account holder, account number, routing number and tax identifier — to any unauthenticated caller, and the same serialiser backs the invoice detail response.

Vendor bank details and invoice history persist in a plain SQLite file that defaults to /tmp/app.db, with no encryption at rest, no access restriction beyond the process, and loss on restart unless the optional persistent disk is enabled (checked: src/main.py:35-65 — the only storage configuration in the tree).

trust_boundaries.name: Committed signing key and provider credential

threats.summary: The Flask SECRET_KEY is a string literal committed in source rather than read from the environment, so the signing key is public to anyone with repository access and identical across every deployment of this code.

The OpenAI credential could have been committed alongside it, but the client is constructed with no inline key and resolves it from the environment, with no API-key literal anywhere in the repository.

Every dependency except Flask is declared as an open-ended floor with no lockfile, SBOM or scanning configuration, so two builds of the same commit can resolve different code and there is no inventory to check when an advisory lands.

The model or language runtime could change silently under the deployment, but the agent targets a concrete model release rather than a floating alias and runtime.txt pins an exact Python patch version.

remit_rules.excerpt: Every invoice decision (approve / reject / route-to-review) MUST be recorded to a durable audit log with its reasoning and confidence.

threats.summary: There is no logging framework, log file or telemetry sink in the tree — only three bare print calls — and the one durable trace, the invoice row's ai_decision/ai_confidence/ai_reasoning, is cleared in place by an unauthenticated reprocess call.

notes.lane_fit: Clean apart from two placements: the stub confidence_threshold control has no enforcing process at all, so it sits in agent_core as the lane of its intended enforcer (the decision path) rather than of the config row it is declared on; and the agent's tools live in the same file as the orchestrator, so finbot_agent.py contributes nodes to both agent_core and tools_mcp.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences (both primary/co-tag ordering shifts on codes the stored finding already carries, not new codes): PRAX-2026-08-12-004 stores LLM01 as its llm primary with ASI01 as an agentic co-tag, but the Agentic KB's 'goal altered by live input' row makes ASI01 primary and LLM01 the co-tag — the graph tags it ASI01. PRAX-2026-08-12-001 lists LLM03 first in its tags array with ASI03 second; the KB's identity/privilege row makes ASI03 the honest primary for an admin control plane exercised by an unauthenticated party — the graph tags it ASI03 at control-plane-exposure and at state-commit. No numbering-only shifts were found; PRAX-2026-08-12-002 (ASI06 per the persistence test) and the null tags on 006, 007, 010 and 013 match the KB as stored, 007 being the KB's 'pure observability gap — RAISE only, no OWASP code' case. Components folded rather than modelled: src/routes/user.py registers an unauthenticated User CRUD blueprint that no finding and no remit rule touches — it is carried as blueprint-registration evidence on main-py-adapter rather than as a node; the marketing and entry static pages (entry, index, leadership, why-partner, ctf-footer.js, agreement-check.js) fold into main-py-adapter's catch-all static evidence; docs/FinBot-CTF-walkthrough-goal-manipulation.md is CTF player material, not an architectural component. Edgeless nodes: confidence-threshold-models-vendor-py-control (declared and writable but read nowhere), secret-key-main-py-secret-store (committed literal, no data flow), requirements-txt-deploy-surface (build-time repo posture). No SCAN_INSTRUCTIONS scope file was present; the whole workspace was treated as the subject. No inter-agent, MCP or peer surface exists in this target, so no peer-a2a boundary was coined.
